study_identification_part.si4_title: Spectral normative modeling of brain structure

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states its objectives: to propose Spectral Normative Modeling (SNM) to overcome limitations of conventional normative modeling at high spatial resolution, and to demonstrate its utility by mapping individualized cortical atrophy patterns and characterizing heterogeneity in Alzheimer's disease. This satisfies both criteria: research aims are defined and the purpose of applying normative modeling is articulated (precision medicine, high-resolution brain charts, clinical demonstration).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "To overcome these key limitations, we propose spectral normative modeling (SNM)... We demonstrate its utility by elucidating high-resolution individual cortical atrophy patterns and characterizing the heterogeneous nature of neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease. SNM lays the groundwork for a new generation of spatially precise brain charts, offering substantial potential to drive advances in individualized precision medicine."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using healthy participants from HCP Lifespan cohorts (HCP-D, HCP-YA, HCP-A). It cites the original HCP publications (meeting the open-dataset citation criterion) and reports final sample sizes and train/test splits. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and image quality/data completeness standards for the reference sample are not detailed in this paper; those details are deferred to the cited HCP sources.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Healthy human brain imaging data from three cohorts of the Human Connectome Project (HCP) was aggregated... Table S.1 summarizes the population demographics across datasets and their respective train-test splits."; "Both models were trained on the same sample of 1,978 healthy individuals... assessed on an independent held-out sample of 495 individuals."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are explicitly modeled in HBR with a spline for age and intercept for sex. Multi-site/dataset effects are handled as batch random effects (harmonization), and results are adjusted for age, sex, and site. Stratified train-test splitting also controls for age, sex, and dataset.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "HBR... aims to model its moments (mean and variance) as a function of covariates (age and sex) while controlling for batch effects."; "adjusted for age, sex, and site effects"; "stratified splitting... utilizing the stratify parameter... discrete values encoding age, sex, and dataset information were utilized for stratified splitting."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described in detail: HBR is used with age modeled via B-splines (df=5), sex intercepts, and hierarchical batch random effects; SNM trains k direct models on eigenmode coefficients. However, software/libraries for implementing HBR/SNM are not explicitly specified (only scikit-learn is mentioned for data splitting), so one criterion is missing.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "we utilize HBR as the normative approach... HBR assumes... modeled as a function of covariates (age and sex) while controlling for batch effects... A B-spline basis expansion (cubic spline with three evenly spaced knots; df=5)... Batch effects... modeled as intercepts... hierarchically modeling batch as a random effect."; "In the training phase, k direct normative models are independently fitted to the projection of phenotypes on the first k brain eigenmodes..."
